State-machine agents: the model only picks a legal event

Agent control flow is a statechart; at each decision the model is shown only the events allowed in the current state and proposes one, the machine validates and transitions, and ready-made machines cover tool loops, routers, supervisors, handoffs and parallel steps, with an event log for replay and resume.

A small flow language and state-machine runtime that pins conversations to designed paths (e.g. authenticate before support), chaining input, dialogue, retrieval, execution and output rails around the model.

When a session goes idle with unfinished todos, a countdown injects a continuation prompt so the agent keeps going, skipping when the user aborted, a question is pending, compaction is running, tokens ran out, or progress has stagnated.
Rubric outcome supervisor with revision loop

A session can carry an outcome with a rubric or rule verifier; after each run a grader decides satisfied, needs_revision (its reason is fed back as the next user message), max_iterations_reached or interrupted, and every verdict is stored with token usage on the session.
Automatic mentor intervention and reflector-guided wind-down

An execution monitor counts identical and total tool calls; past a threshold it automatically asks an adviser agent (optionally a stronger model) to analyse progress and appends its advice to the tool result, and near the hard tool-call limit a reflector steers the agent to finish cleanly. The authors measured about 2x better results for a 27B local model.

Failures are retried at the lowest layer that can fix them (tool call, backend, agent runtime, gateway daemon), each with bounded attempts and a cleanup deadline, and only escalate upward when a unit stops making progress; overload is handled separately by lowering caps.
Render old history as images to cut tokens

Moves long text (older history, tool schemas) into rendered PNG image blocks for Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini requests when a density gate says it saves tokens; the original text stays recoverable and any error falls back to plain text.

Context is selected under a token budget (knapsack over fragments) and every omitted piece gets a receipt and a content-addressed handle so the agent or user can recover the exact original bytes later and see what was kept or dropped and why.
Content-aware tool-output compression with retrievable originals

Detects whether a tool result is a log, JSON, diff, HTML, code listing, search results or a table and shrinks it with a matching compressor; every original is stored in a local SQLite store so the agent can pull the full bytes back by query.
ObservationPack: stable handles for repeated large tool results
Large tool outputs that would be replayed in later requests are replaced by stable handles kept in a local ledger, with exact paged recall when the model needs the text again.
Deterministic layered token-compression codec for tool observations

A no-model-call compression pipeline shrinks prompts and tool observations through stacked lossless-style layers (deduplication, a static and a dynamic codebook/dictionary, JSON compaction, path and whitespace folding), cutting tokens before the request goes out.
A cheap helper model condenses long diagnostic logs into a compact receipt, accepted only if every quoted line exactly matches the archived original; otherwise the full result is kept.
Agent-directed context reduction by message tags

Every message and tool result gets a short tag; the agent calls ctx_reduce to drop or shrink tagged items it no longer needs and ctx_expand to bring a compressed item back, so the context is trimmed surgically instead of by a compaction pause.
Cost-aware compaction decision (cache invalidation vs savings)

Before compacting, the engine estimates whether the token savings outweigh the cost of invalidating and rewriting the prompt cache, and adjusts the target from measured context growth, so compaction runs only when it pays.
Typed AI functions (cast, classify, extract, generate, @fn)

One-call helpers that turn free text into a given type: cast to a schema, classify into an enum or label list, extract all values of a type, generate N typed items, summarize, and @fn to give a plain function signature an LLM body. Useful as building blocks for automations and skills.
AI-slop detector and writing quality gate

Scores text for tells of bland AI writing (hedging openers, stock vocabulary, negative parallelism, em-dash overuse) per 1,000 words and returns pass/warn/fail with relaxed, balanced and strict presets calibrated on a blog corpus.
Non-LLM goal planner that replans after every action

Typed actions declare preconditions and effects; an A* GOAP planner (or a utility planner) finds an action sequence to the goal, replans after each action from the new world state, prunes irrelevant actions and detects unreachable goals, so flows can combine known steps in new orders without asking the model to plan.

Rules constrain the loop: a tool may only run after another, must run at a given step, has a call limit or consecutive-call limit, or needs the user's permission first; the runner enforces them each step so the agent follows a reliable procedure without a hard-coded workflow.
Overnight autonomous runs with a morning report

A background 'overnight' run manager (start/status/log/review/cancel) with a manifest that tracks wake time, a coordinator session and a morning report posted when the owner wakes, so the agent works unattended overnight and reports back.
Endless continuation: auto next steps, ideas and goals

Opt-in modes where, after each reply, the agent automatically continues with the next logical steps (including tests), dreams up and implements improvement ideas for the codebase, or, when a /goal is met, writes and starts the next goal.
Batched command run with output bindings

The model sends one command_run containing several shell, patch and planning steps where later steps reference earlier outputs through placeholders; the runtime executes the whole chain (streaming, with file locks) without another model round trip, cutting tokens sharply on coding tasks.

Before any work starts the agent interviews the user, scores remaining ambiguity with evidence after each answer, tracks answer provenance and 'decide later' items, and only crystallizes a testable spec (seed with acceptance criteria) once ambiguity falls below a threshold.
Read the room: friction signals change agent behaviour

A deterministic lexical reader scores each owner message for friction (caps, 'still broken', repeated corrections, interrupts, denials, urgency) and a reducer turns it into a policy: act on corrections at once and narrowly, explore when curious, get terse when urgent, and weigh forceful instructions more in memory.
Desires that drive autonomous heartbeat time

The agent keeps a store of its own desires; the heartbeat picks an actionable one to focus on, pursues it, records activity, and desires evolve or are reviewed over time, so scheduled autonomous time has its own motivation besides standing chores.
One protocol over many agent harnesses, with a conformance suite

Codex, Claude Code, OpenHands, Aider, Hermes, Gemini CLI and others run behind one Responses-style API with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation and structured failure reasons, and a published protocol with a conformance test kit checks each harness adapter.
Per-step persona switch with relevance-filtered history

Each loop iteration predicts the best next step, picks the best-fit persona (researcher, developer, CSV analyst, synthesizer) for it, and rebuilds the chat history from only the chunks most relevant to that prediction before deciding which function to run.

Keeps the model's full reasoning only for the most recent turns and asks it to carry forward short notes in normal content, so long multi-turn coding runs keep deep thinking without the context exploding.

At a chosen decision point the agent generates K candidates in parallel, scores each with a check (for example running the tests) and keeps the highest-scoring one instead of committing to a single answer.

A /harness command swaps the whole agent harness (system prompt, tool set and schemas, compaction prompt, guidance) to emulate Claude Code, Kimi Code, Kimi CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Pi, SWE-agent, mini-SWE-agent, Terminus and others, with routing that picks the harness a given model performs best in.
Process-as-code orchestration with journal replay, forking and breakpoints

A workflow is a JS process file whose task, parallel, sleep, subprocess and breakpoint calls are recorded in an append-only run journal; each iteration replays the journal to a deterministic point, so runs resume, fork from any step and stop at human approval breakpoints while the coding agent just executes the next pending effect.
Sentinel autopilot: nudge, escalate to a person, or stop when a long run parks

When the lead agent pauses before its goal is done, a classifier decides whether to nudge it onward, escalate a genuine blocker to the owner over Telegram or Slack with a resume token, or treat the goal as done; off by default and enabled per team.
Hook sandbox: dry-run a hook with simulated input

Pick any configured hook, feed it a simulated event payload and see its stdout, stderr, exit code and transformed result, run in an isolated environment with only PATH/HOME/TMPDIR and no API tokens or credentials, plus validation of the hook definition.
Backfill a schedule over past dates
A scheduled trigger can be backfilled for a chosen past date range, creating the runs that would have happened, with pause/resume and a banner showing backfill progress.

For a big coding task the agent first interviews the owner in batches of questions with a follow-up budget, compiles a PRD, splits it into atomic 'beads' with a dependency graph and coverage revision, executes each bead in an isolated worktree loop with a completion checker, then generates and runs a final test pass with a file-effects audit.
Focus items with agent-managed bound triggers

The agent keeps a list of focus items it is tracking and must bind every task trigger it creates (cron, once, interval, HTTP poll, on-message from a given agent or person, webhook) to a focus item; it adjusts its own triggers as work evolves and cancels them when the focus is completed.
Discover automatable workflows from recorded activity

A scheduled discovery agent reviews the captured screen and audio history, finds repeated work the user does, and proposes workflows with step evidence that the user can accept, run and share; an eval script scores discovery quality.
Application tracker with follow-up cadence and funnel stats
A tracker of every evaluated and applied job with dedup and repost detection, follow-up reminders on a cadence after the applied date, and funnel velocity and discard analytics in a TUI dashboard.
Proactive sentinel that learns routines and predicts tasks

Attention producers (active threads, project rhythm, recently abandoned work, daily plan, rejected-offer cooldown) feed a routine learner and task discoverer; a planner tick decides whether to nudge or act, derives do-not-disturb windows, defers, and tracks feedback on each offer.
Agent-owned outcomes over weeks with reviews, metrics and owner action items

Hand one lead agent an outcome with a definition of done and optional metrics; it turns it into roadmap tasks and schedules, reviews progress on a cadence recording evidence and next steps, files access requests for missing capabilities and action items for things only the owner can do, and can only propose completion; the owner marks it done.
Public form and chat page that starts an automation and returns its answer
A form trigger or chat trigger gives an automation its own web page; whoever fills the form or chats starts the run, and a 'return response' step sends the result back to that page.

A Markdown playbook is co-written with the agent and run from the same document: regions are marked, verbs such as interview, simplify, challenge-assumptions and crystallize act on them, and runs report back into the document.
Typed runbooks compiled into skills with resumable checkpoints

A YAML runbook declares steps (agent, script, loop, parallel, branch) whose inputs and outputs are JSON-schema files; a compiler checks the contracts close and the graph has no cycles, then emits a SKILL.md plus checkpoint scripts so a broken run resumes at the last finished step.
Scheduled-job pipeline graph and weekly heatmap
Declares pipelines as edges between scheduled jobs (job A's artifact feeds job B), draws them as a DAG with health per job, and shows a weekly heatmap of when jobs fire.
Track published posts and run a daily retro
Every published post is recorded in a local database; a scheduled job fetches views, likes and comments per platform, flags pending or failed publishes, and feeds a daily review of what worked.
Nestable reusable blocks usable in any text field

A library of named blocks (plain text, prompt, code, module call or whole workflow) that can be referenced from any prompt or text field and nest inside each other, so shared instructions and computed values are reused consistently.
Scheduled social engagement in the owner's voice with per-platform limits

A scheduler runs one agent per social platform (LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Bluesky, Threads, Medium, Dev.to and more) in its own signed-in browser profile, following the owner's identity, voice and content strategy, with daily per-platform action limits, a run lock and a quality audit of what was posted.
Auto Run playbooks over markdown checklists

Point the agent at a folder of markdown task documents; each unchecked item runs in a fresh session with clean context, gets ticked off with a synopsis, documents can loop, human-only steps pause with a banner, and saved playbooks run headless from the CLI or cron.
Recorded phone macros with guarded replay and agent hand-off
Record a task as a macro, then replay it step by step only while the screen matches the recorded state; on a mismatch the run hands off to the agent to recover instead of tapping blindly.
Meeting prep briefs before calendar meetings

A scheduler watches the calendar and, before each meeting, writes a prep brief from what the knowledge graph knows about the attendees and topics, and notifies the user; a popup also detects a meeting starting.

Polls a watchlist of social accounts within set hours and a spend budget, scores fresh posts for relevance, retrieves the owner's context and drafts suggested replies that are delivered for review and never posted automatically.
Cost estimate for a recurring agent routine before enabling it

Estimates a routine's monthly token spend from its cadence, how often runs are no-op, report or action at its autonomy level, and the share of stable cacheable context, so the owner sees the cost before switching it on.
Real-time co-editing of a workflow with cursors and comment threads
Several people edit the same workflow at once through a CRDT over WebSocket, see each other's cursors in their own colours, and leave threaded comments with @mentions pinned to places on the canvas.

A daily notes page (also a desktop HUD/pill) where writing a task item or mentioning the assistant gets picked up within minutes; a proactive observer agent also reads the page and leaves inline comments or drafts a plan, without the user opening a chat.
Each scheduled job keeps up to 20 deduplicated lessons its runs saved (oldest dropped first), which are given to the next run so recurring jobs stop repeating mistakes.
A workflow step that collects events for a subscriber over a time window (regular or with backoff, or on a schedule) and sends one combined notification instead of many.
Split a failing multi-part task into child tasks (mitosis)
When a task holding several deliverables fails the first time, it is split into focused child tasks linked as dependencies, deduplicated against existing children under a workspace lock.
Deep-work projects that assign steps to the human

A goal is parsed into a project plan whose tasks are split between agents and the human; dependent tasks are scheduled, and human-required tasks are pushed to the owner's chat apps and wait for him before downstream agent work continues.
Feed subscriptions that post new items into chats
Owners subscribe a chat channel to RSS, Reddit or YouTube feeds; a poller fetches with rate limits and posts each new item as a message, tracked per subscription so nothing repeats.
Inbox work loops with ship gates and a health governor

Long-running loops pull items from Gmail or Slack into a ledger, triage them and prepare outputs (labels, reply drafts); each outgoing action is held for the owner unless a declared policy or a revocable grant allows it, and a governor quarantines, throttles or pings when a loop's queue or outputs look unhealthy.
Two-way sync between visual agent builder and TypeScript code

Agents built on the visual canvas can be pulled as TypeScript files and edited in code, then pushed back; pulling again merges into existing files, preserving comments, key order and variable names, and reports conflicts.
Brain dump triage into an Eisenhower matrix
The owner dumps raw ideas; an agent triages them into tasks placed on an urgent/important matrix (Do, Schedule, Delegate, Eliminate) that can be dragged between quadrants and delegated to agents.
Weekly work report from git and calendar
Collects the owner's week from GitHub or local git activity and Google Calendar events, and writes a progress report with achievements, ongoing work and plans.
Call tools a web page exposes through WebMCP

When a page registers WebMCP tools, the browser agent discovers them (including in frames and late registrations), validates input against their schemas, invokes and cancels them with size and count limits, and notices when the page context changes under it, so it can use the site's own actions instead of clicking.
WebMCP bridge: expose tools to browser-native agents
Bridges an agent's MCP tools (plus in-page tools) to Chrome's navigator.modelContext so agents built into the browser can discover and call them directly from the page.
Browser action receipts with failure kind and next command

Every click, fill, press or navigate returns a one-line receipt (URL, outcome, dialogs, downloads); a failed action names a typed kind such as covered, disabled or stale-ref plus a runnable next command, and clicks wait for actionability and refuse to land on a covering element.
Point at page elements and leave comments as instructions

In the agent's browser panel the person switches to annotate mode, clicks or drags over page elements and attaches comments (up to 24); the annotated elements and notes are sent to the agent as inspect, change or review instructions.
In-page agent via one script tag (text DOM, no screenshots)

Drop one script into any web page and it gets its own agent that reads a compact text DOM tree and clicks, types and scrolls in place with a visible simulated cursor, plus React/antd input patches; no extension, headless browser or vision model needed.
Simulate candidate web actions before acting

For each candidate click or type on a page, a model imagines the resulting page state a few steps ahead and scores progress toward the goal; the agent executes only the best-scoring action, avoiding irreversible mistakes.
Bounded table extraction from live pages

Pulls whole tables and virtualized grids out of a page into row artifacts, with row identity from aria-rowindex or a key column, sampling, and an explicit stop reason (row, byte, time or no-progress limit) so partial results are honest.

The agent can tie each browser action to the requests, response bodies, console messages and page changes it caused, find slow or duplicate API calls, apply explicit HTTP rules or replay a request to test a hypothesis, and export the redacted evidence as JSON.
Agent web-security workbench (capture, edit-and-replay, diff HTTP traffic)

An agent can browse a target with capture on, list captured requests, resend one with edited fields, diff two responses and run request sequences/matrices to hunt for vulnerabilities, with findings recorded.
Agent Window and borrow-a-tab in the owner's browser

Agent tasks in the owner's real browser run in their own visible window so the owner keeps working; an existing tab can be borrowed only after an on-page confirmation and is handed back when the task ends, with cleanup on disconnect.
Declutter pages and flag dark patterns for the agent

Hides cookie banners, ads (EasyList), chat widgets, newsletter modals and footers to save tokens (~11% measured), and annotates manipulative patterns such as confirm-shaming, fake scarcity, countdown timers, hidden fees, pre-ticked checkout boxes, spoofed links and hard-to-cancel flows so the agent is not steered by them.
Layout-preserving text rendering of a page for text-only models

Interactable (or all text) elements are tagged in the page with bracketed ids, and an OCR pass turns the tagged screenshot into whitespace-structured text that keeps the visual layout, so a model without vision can act on ids like CLICK [23]; works with Playwright and Selenium.
Chrome performance-trace insight extraction for agents

Records a Chrome performance trace, chunk-parses it and distills actionable performance insights (slow phases, bottlenecks) into a compact form an agent can read, alongside network and console tools whose output is formatted with source-mapped stack traces.
Passkeys (WebAuthn) for websites in the embedded browser
Sites opened in the built-in browser can register and sign in with platform passkeys through a native bridge, with a policy on which origins may use them.

Turns any Telegram file into an HTTP link that streams with range requests straight from Telegram over MTProto, using several worker bots, so files above the Bot API's download limit work without first downloading them.
Steer terminal agent sessions from a chat app

Telegram, Feishu or WeChat get a card when a session waits (which session, what for, Allow/Deny buttons); replying 'N: text' types into session N, 'shot N' returns a picture of the pane, and in advanced mode a plain request is routed to the right session and typed only after the user says ok.
The assistant joins a live stream's chat, reads viewer comments and gifts (Bilibili danmaku over websocket, YouTube and Twitch live chat) and answers them as the on-screen character.
Chat-to-chat forwarding and live sync with transform plugins

Rules forward messages from source chats to destination chats, either all past messages or live from now, passing each through plugins: whitelist/blacklist filter, regex replace, formatting, header/footer captions, image/video watermark and OCR.
One Slack app per agent, provisioned automatically

Setup creates a separate Slack app for each agent (manifest, avatar, workspace install) so every agent has its own bot identity with no tokens to paste, and agents can open shared rooms and write room canvases.
Cloud stand-in keeps the bot answering while the PC is off

A free Cloudflare Worker takes over the same Telegram bot when the home PC stops checking in, answers and queues work, then hands the bot back when the PC starts, with phone approvals relayed through it.
Owner-written custom chat commands in a sandboxed template language

Server owners write custom commands triggered by text, reactions, slash commands, components or intervals in a Go-template language with a per-command key-value database and execution limits, edited in a web panel.
Evidence-based stuck detector for delegated coding agents

Watches an external coding agent process and decides whether it is working, waiting or truly stuck from tiered evidence (output activity, workspace changes, live sub-agents, repetition), so it never kills an agent doing real sub-agent work, plus a post-exit verdict.
Executable architecture and behavior contracts as the done gate

Project rules live in the repo as contracts: static structure rules checked over the code with tree-sitter (Python, TS, Go, Java, Rust, C), and runtime behavior rules checked with generated inputs and minimized counterexamples; `status` says GREEN or BLOCKED and the agent cannot finish while red.

A task the agent marks closed is only accepted if a commit touching real files (not notes) was made since dispatch and pushed upstream, or the agent wrote a note explaining why no change was needed; repeated fake closures quarantine the task instead of looping.
Acceptance bound to a verification fingerprint

Verification runs separately from the task and is fingerprinted with the exact diff; a review gate and the human acceptance step are tied to that fingerprint, so accepting stale or changed work is refused and an attestation is recorded.
Decision memory keyed by code entity, injected before edits

Agents record why an approach was chosen, what was rejected and what would change their mind, keyed to a function, route or dependency; a pre-tool hook surfaces those records when the agent is about to edit that code.
Failover between coding agents with failure budgets

Classifies each delegated-agent failure (connectivity, unavailability, same-shape repeated failure), spends per-agent failure budgets with cycle caps, and fails over to another configured coding CLI with a retry prompt.
PR babysitting: watch CI and rerun only proven-flaky jobs
Opt a PR into /baby-sit and the agent watches its CI through webhooks, diagnoses each failure, fixes real breakages and reruns only jobs whose failure evidence shows they are flaky.
Proactive coding buddy with codebase-health observers

A background companion runs observers (diagnostic clusters, git pressure, worktree hygiene, provider health, MCP auth, customization drift, trajectory clutter) and scheduled jobs (daily digest, Friday retro, idle suggestions, refactor hunter, test-coverage watcher, PR-issue matchmaker, error triage, self-critic), and a speech policy decides when it may speak up.

Watches a work tracker (Linear, Jira, GitHub, GitLab or Asana), gives each eligible issue its own isolated workspace (locally or over SSH) and a Codex app-server run governed by a repo WORKFLOW.md, retries with backoff, and returns proof of work (CI status, PR review feedback) on the issue, with a status dashboard; a language-neutral SPEC.md lets you re-implement it.

File reads tag each line with a short content hash and edits address lines by number plus hash, so edits against stale content are detected and recovered instead of silently mis-applied; sloppy and apply_patch modes share one engine.
Phased feature pipeline from goal to PR with review gates

A big feature runs as fixed stages: build a repo knowledge base, inquiry questions, research by specialist researcher agents, design, a roadmap, per-phase plans (tracer bullet first, then TDD fill-ins), plan validators, implementation with review axes, final fix and PR description; optional owner gates pause at each review and 'need user input' points.
Blast-radius query on a static code graph
Builds a static import/symbol graph with layers and health checks and answers 'what is affected if I change this file' before an agent edits.
Affected tests and dead code from the code graph

Given changed files, the graph lists the tests that exercise them (with per-language test conventions), and it reports unreferenced code, so the agent runs only relevant tests and can prune dead code.
Finds unreferenced functions, classes and exports using the symbol index, aware of dynamic imports, intra-file calls and JS re-exports, evaluated against a labeled corpus.
Runs passing and failing tests with coverage to rank the statements most likely to hold the bug (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, Rust backends) and fuses that with other signals before the agent edits.
Co-change coupling and change-impact prediction from git history
Answers 'what always changes together' and 'what breaks if I touch this' by mining git history for co-change with per-type half-life decay plus counterfactual removal over the code graph.
Find the same bug shape elsewhere (antibodies)
After a fix, the bug's structural pattern is stored as an 'antibody' and the graph is scanned for other places with the same shape.
Speculative edit sessions with diagnostic delta
The agent previews an edit in memory, gets the before/after diagnostics difference from the real language server, and only then applies or discards it, so broken edits never touch disk.
Installs and supervises a worker inside IDA so the agent can query and annotate disassembly of binaries through tools.

The agent edits code by symbol instead of line numbers: replace a function or class body, insert before/after a symbol, rename a symbol across the whole project and safely delete a symbol only when nothing references it, with diagnostics returned after each edit and atomic file writes.
Action fusion: edit plus validation in one call
An edit or write tool call can carry its follow-up validation command (tests, lint, build), which runs right after the write in the same call, removing a model round-trip per edit.

While the agent is fixing failing checks, writes to test files are refused by default (or flagged), so it must fix the code or say the test is wrong; a test changed after a failure is reported next to any 'verified' result so green never hides a rewritten test.
Check bonds: prove each passing check can fail

Before trusting a pass, the verifier briefly adds fixtures that must make each check fail; a check that still passes, or whose test configuration the change itself edited, is reported as untrusted instead of green.

Common TypeScript errors in generated code (cannot find name, missing module, missing exported member, default/named import mismatches) are repaired by AST rules that add imports, fix paths or create stubs, without a model call.
Stage mode: agent writes held in an overlay until applied
The coding agent's file writes go into a staged queue that its own later reads see as an overlay; nothing touches disk until the user applies, CRLF is preserved and the queue survives restart.
Guided tour of an agent's changes

A button turns a task's diff (or a file) into a step-by-step tour with explanations, suggested questions, threads and an ask bar, so the user can understand and question what the agent changed before merging.
After the first review, the tool generates check questions per finding, answers them against the code, scores each issue and drops likely false positives before reporting.
SAST scan fed into AI review
Downloads OpenGrep on demand, scans the changed code, trims its JSON to the fields the model needs and gives it to the reviewer with guidance.
Vulnerability research scans with ranked, validated findings

Breaks a repository security review into small prompt steps run in parallel by coding-agent CLIs, merges output into one finding schema with candidate dedupe, ranks severity with editable rankers, runs post-scripts that try to prove each issue (PoC, report), and exports a share-safe ZIP.
Coverage-verified security review with a checked ledger and SARIF

A parser cuts C/C++ code into units that each review agent must answer fixed questions about; a checker re-derives the spots from source and marks the run unverified if an agent skipped any, then findings are assembled into a report and SARIF.
Token-budgeted compression of large PR diffs

Large pull requests are fitted into the model's budget by extending hunks with context, dropping deletion-only hunks, sorting files by language and token weight, and clipping or splitting into several calls, so reviews still work on huge diffs.
PR command toolkit across git hosts

Comment commands on a PR: /describe writes title, summary and labels; /improve posts committable code suggestions with inline-comment dedup; /ask and line questions; /update_changelog; ticket compliance checks against the linked issue; all through one provider interface for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gerrit, Gitea and CodeCommit.
Cross-model adversarial review of a diff

After the main model writes a change, a model from a different family (Codex, GPT or Gemini via OpenRouter) red-teams the same diff against the spec, reporting only correctness, requirement and invariant gaps with file:line; disagreements are shown to the user, and a skipped review gets its own exit code so it is never mistaken for a pass.
Whole-repo semantic drift audit with parallel rubric reviewers

Scans a whole repository, dispatches focused reviewers (stale docs, spec vs code, duplicate/orphan files, conventions, i18n sync, icons) in parallel, consolidates and dedupes findings with evidence and severity, and produces a self-contained HTML report; never edits files.
Upserted GitHub tracking issue for recurring audit findings
Scheduled CI audits find their previous tracking issue by a stable hash marker and update it in place instead of opening duplicates, so recurring findings live in one issue.
Architecture decision records retrieved and enforced

Imports and compiles the project's ADRs into a decision index; relevant decisions are retrieved into the coding agent's context, governed rules are enforced deterministically on proposed changes by path selectors, and conflicts, staleness and decision authority are checked.
Deterministic UI quality detector for generated frontends

A rule engine scans generated UI code for AI-slop tells (purple gradients by hue, generic patterns, accessibility misses) with severities, one-line fixes, auto-fix for some rules and a 0-100 score that can gate CI or a review hook.
PR reviewer that learns the repository's review style

An automatic or on-demand PR reviewer publishes findings to GitHub, then collects how maintainers reacted to past findings and review comments to build per-repository style guidance that shapes later reviews; outcomes are reconciled and evaluated.
Compiler-verified backend builder (requirements to DB, API, tests and code)

From a chat description the agent runs a waterfall of phases (analyze requirements, design database schema, design API, write e2e tests, implement) where each phase emits an AST that a compiler validates and the agent corrects until it builds.
Dependency upgrade agent that fixes breaking changes

Bumps a package to a target version, builds the project to collect errors, uses the TypeScript AST and the new package's type signatures to build a dependency/plan graph, then edits affected code in order until the build passes; can run on Dependabot/Renovate PRs.
Issue to failing test to execution-selected fix

From an issue URL it writes a regression test that fails, samples several candidate patches, keeps the one that passes the real test suite (after a static blast-radius check), and opens a PR from a fork; every phase is checkpointed so a crash resumes.
Backprop runtime failures into the spec

A post-tool hook spots failing test runs and queues a backprop step; the gap becomes a new numbered acceptance criterion plus a regression test before the loop resumes, so a bug found late tightens the spec instead of just being patched.
Staged evaluation pipeline with reward-hacking veto

Finished work is judged in stages: mechanical checks run real commands, a semantic judge checks acceptance criteria, then multi-model consensus with reviewer independence; an adversarial pass and a reward-hacking veto reject work that games the checks, and the grading command is never shown to the worker.
Risk-tiered pipeline with automatic security review

A deterministic (no LLM) classifier rates each task low/normal/high/security from keywords and paths; low risk takes a fast path while anything touching auth, crypto or network adds a dedicated security audit stage before the branch is cut.
Test-first enforcement hook for coding agents

A pre-edit hook sends each proposed write/edit plus the latest test results (from reporters for Vitest, Jest, pytest, Go, Rust, PHPUnit and more) to a validator model, and blocks implementation that has no failing test or goes beyond it; a post-edit hook enforces lint during refactor; can be toggled per session.
Executor/supervisor task runner with focused retries

Pick a cheap executor model and a separate supervisor model per task; the supervisor checks acceptance criteria then repo quality policy, keeps already-verified passes and points the next attempt only at unresolved items, with every attempt's plan, output, checks and diff kept for inspection.
Which session made a commit (multi-session commit provenance)

In a checkout shared by several agent sessions, records which session ran each git commit and which sessions' file writes are inside it, separating authored commits from fast-forwards, without writing trailers or notes.
Verified handover passport for AI-built projects

Scans the repo and Claude Code/Codex/Cursor history for facts, claims and decisions, runs install/build/test in a Docker sandbox, and writes a digest-stamped passport where every statement has a truth status and evidence; the recipient re-runs the checks with one command and any divergence is named.
Narrows an issue to the files, then the classes/functions, then the exact edit locations using a compressed repo skeleton plus embedding retrieval, before any code is written.
Magic commands: resolve merge conflicts and investigate security alerts

One-click commands hand the agent a prepared task: resolve the current branch's merge conflicts, investigate a GitHub security alert, Dependabot advisory or Sentry issue, address review comments or update a PR, each with its own configurable prompt, model and effort.
Pre-trust new worktrees for Claude Code and Codex

Before spawning a worker in a fresh worktree, writes the trust entry into ~/.claude.json or passes a Codex -c trust override, so dispatched agents don't stall on the workspace-trust dialog; a PTY auto-answer stays as fallback.
Auto-merge of parallel worker worktrees with conflict mailbox

When several helper agents work in separate worktrees, a merge coordinator merges finished work back in order, and any conflict is posted to the responsible worker's mailbox to resolve instead of stalling the team; survives restarts.
